audits.claim: A valid backup code plus any nonempty totpCode authenticates a CAL user without verifying their password.
audits.evidence: For a CAL user with a password, twoFactorEnabled=true and an unused backup code, submit email, password="", totpCode="x" and that backupCode to the credentials provider declared in packages/features/auth/lib/next-auth-options.ts:57-67. The CAL identity passes the guards at lines 113-119, and the nonempty totpCode skips password verification at lines 121-129. The backup-code branch at lines 131-156 accepts and consumes the valid code, bypassing the TOTP validation in the mutually exclusive branch at lines 157-185, and returns the authenticated user at lines 205-214. The signIn callback explicitly accepts credentials at lines 523-529, so there is no later password guard; the login form validation does not protect a direct credentials request.

audits.claim: Dismissing the backup-code step with Escape or an outside click skips the success callback, leaving the settings status stale and the modal step unreset.
audits.evidence: apps/web/pages/api/auth/two-factor/totp/enable.ts:56-65 commits twoFactorEnabled=true before returning success, but apps/web/components/settings/EnableTwoFactorModal.tsx:134-136 now only selects DisplayBackupCodes. The Dialog forwards onOpenChange directly at line 166, and packages/ui/components/dialog/Dialog.tsx:70 and 87-104 use Radix Root/Content without preventing Escape or outside dismissal. On that path, apps/web/pages/settings/security/two-factor-auth.tsx:64 only toggles modal visibility; the query invalidation is exclusively in onEnable at lines 65-67, while the switch and badge still derive from the cached user at lines 46 and 54-55. The explicit Close handler alone resets the step and invokes onEnable (EnableTwoFactorModal.tsx:266-270), so dismissing and reopening without a query refresh displays the old backup-code step and an off status despite enabled server state; a later window-focus refetch can repair the status but does not refute this path.

audits.claim: The missing-backup-codes login error directs users who have lost their authenticator to settings that require an authenticated session.
audits.evidence: packages/prisma/migrations/20230804153419_add_backup_codes/migration.sql:2 adds a nullable backupCodes column without backfilling existing 2FA users. Such a CAL user can enter a correct password, choose Lost access (apps/web/pages/auth/login.tsx:120-129), and submit a nonempty backup code, causing MissingBackupCodes at packages/features/auth/lib/next-auth-options.ts:137 and the settings instruction at login.tsx:158 and apps/web/public/static/locales/en/common.json:2019. Generating codes actually requires a session (apps/web/pages/api/auth/two-factor/totp/setup.ts:18-20), and setup rejects an already-enabled account at lines 42-43, so the proposed recovery instruction is unusable for someone who has lost their authenticator and has no remaining session. This is misleading recovery copy rather than a newly caused authentication lockout: TOTP login remains available to users who retain the authenticator, and the new message itself does not remove a working recovery method.
